target_customer: Retailers, restaurants, healthcare providers and logistics firms wanting drone last-mile delivery
problem: Last-mile delivery of small packages and medical supplies is slow and costly, especially to remote places.
business_model: Drone delivery service, later hardware and patent licensing as SkyDrop

founders.name: Matt Sweeny
founders.background_notes: YC page: inventor on 11 US drone patents and partnered with NASA, enterprise sales including 7-Eleven, FedEx and Domino's. Education and employers not listed.

exit.reason: Funding ran out and the company filed Chapter 7 after failing to secure a soft landing, per founder LinkedIn post reported by DroneDJ.

competitors.name: Amazon Prime Air
competitors.what: Amazon was pushing the FAA for permission to test drone delivery
competitors.traction_then: Had not been approved for the mission Flirtey completed

technical_complexity.rationale: Autonomous drone flight and payload release with safety and FAA approval, hardware plus software for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: First FAA approved delivery and drone patents gave a head start, but regulation was a shared barrier and big firms had more money.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: TechCrunch 2017 called Alphabet and Amazon potentially stiffer competition; Flirtey itself later shut down in 2024 as funding ran out.

market_need_then: Amazon announced drone delivery plans and fought the FAA for approval, and the July 2015 Virginia flight cut a 90 minute drive to 3 minutes for a rural clinic.

branding.brand_signature: First FAA approved US drone delivery; drone in the Smithsonian

rebrands.why: Strategy shift toward selling and licensing hardware, software and patents to operators

branding.community_and_virality: Press coverage of the 2015 Virginia delivery and the 7-Eleven partnership.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong press milestones but the playful name was dropped in 2022 and the company still ran out of money.

pivots.to: OEM seller and licensor of hardware, software and patents (SkyDrop)
pivots.why: Company said it would focus on selling and licensing to leading operators

outcome_analysis: Flirtey won early firsts, including the July 2015 FAA approved delivery, and raised a 16 million dollar Series A in 2017, but later struggled to secure funding and partnerships. It rebranded to SkyDrop in 2022, tried to open source its kit, and filed Chapter 7 in February 2024 as funding ran out.
notes: Directory status says Active but sources report Chapter 7 shutdown in Feb 2024; conflict flagged. YC page claims 40M raised at 120M valuation, not verified so not recorded as a round. Valqari patent purchase is from one aggregator only, unverified. Seed date Oct 2015 appeared in a search summary only so the date is just 2015. Flirtey.com redirects to an unrelated site, treated as dead. Matternet and Zipline appear only in 2017 coverage, too late for as_of. Name origin not found.
